title: Integration test: auth rejection paths
description:
What: Integration tests for auth rejection paths: (1) unknown identity gets 401, (2) peer calling owner-only method gets forbiddenMethod error, (3) Peer/deliver with mismatched senderTailscaleUserId is rejected with zero DB writes. All use a single real TCP kithd instance via spawn_test_listener.

Algorithm:
1. Spawn ONE alice kithd instance via spawn_test_listener(state, data_dir)
   Alice's MockWhoIs maps:
   - 127.0.0.1:PORT_OWNER -> alice owner identity (uid-alice)
   - 127.0.0.1:PORT_PEER -> bob peer identity (uid-bob, in contacts)
   - (any other IP) -> WhoIsFailed (unknown)
   For tests to simulate different callers: use two different source port connections — but with loopback, the test client controls what IP is reported. Actually: MockWhoIs must be keyed by full SocketAddr, not just IP. Tests will use separate local sockets. Alternatively: use the existing e2e.rs oneshot pattern with MockConnectInfo to inject different peer addresses without real TCP.
   Decision: use oneshot() pattern (not real TCP) for KITH-szi since auth logic is fully testable in-process and the rejection tests do not need the delivery path.

2. Test (1) — Unknown identity → 401:
   Inject MockConnectInfo with an addr that MockWhoIs returns WhoIsFailed for.
   Send JMAP request: POST /jmap/api with valid body.
   Assert HTTP 401, body={"type":"unauthorized"}, no PII.

3. Test (2) — Peer calls owner-only method:
   Inject MockConnectInfo with bob's addr (bob is in contacts as a Peer).
   Send JMAP request: POST /jmap/api with Message/set or Contact/get.
   Assert HTTP 200 with methodResponse error type='forbiddenMethod'.

4. Test (3) — Peer/deliver with mismatched senderTailscaleUserId:
   Inject MockConnectInfo with bob's addr (WhoIs returns uid-bob).
   Send Peer/deliver request body with senderTailscaleUserId='uid-eve' (mismatch).
   Assert: error response with type='invalidArguments'.
   INDEPENDENT ORACLE: read message state counter from store directly BEFORE and AFTER the request.
   Assert: state counter unchanged (s-0 before and after = no row was inserted).

Defensive programming:
- Never use the same identity for both the caller AND the expectedSender in test (3)
- Test (3) must verify DB state BEFORE the request as the baseline, not assume s-0
- No PII check: assert error body does not contain email addresses or user IDs

Agent team: R (read e2e.rs existing patterns) + I (implement using oneshot) + T (independent oracle: state counter) + V (cargo test -p kithd)

Tests: Three named test functions with clear conditions and independent oracles
